area.title: What are you importing: commodity search and selection
area.scope: Commodity and species selection for live animals and germinal products: the commodity search, its results and the selection panel, the commodity and species lists, removing a chosen commodity or species, and the commodity reference service behind them. Stops at the commodity details page (commodity-details), animal identification and the reason for import. Includes the high-risk plants frontend commodity type page and commodity vocabulary and its commodity rulings, where a row changes the same page plants also has.

sources.role: the answers to the two notification view header questions the 25 November re-distil raised from ruling:sam-2026-11-19 point 2. It settles c-438: once the amend confirmation page exists, 'Amend this notification' on the header is a link to that page rather than a posting button, because the first click then changes nothing, a POST that only renders a page is the wrong verb and leaves a re-POST on the back button without JavaScript, and Delete already opens its confirmation page by href in the same header; Copy as new keeps its own form because it still changes something, Delete stays a link, and no action shares another's form, in live animals, germinal products and plants alike. Point 2 of the 19 November ruling is unweakened, its subject being that no action shares another action's form, which a link does not do. It settles c-447 the other way from the default: the plants header gains a Copy as new action so both journeys offer the same three actions. That is wiring rather than a feature build, because every layer beneath it is already on main - the plants backend serves POST /{referenceNumber}/copy with a NotificationCopyMapper, the plants frontend's real and stub persistence both implement copy, and its engine holds copyJourney - and only the header's copyAction and route are missing. The plants backend therefore needs nothing and trade-imports-plants-backend does not join this programme's repos; inc-123 takes plantsfrontend alongside backend, frontend and tests, and inc-124's stale-copy return takes plants too. Plants' copy carries plants' own answers, so the carried-over-trade against cleared-shipment split is read against plants' own fields rather than copied field for field.

sources.role: the decision that pagination is kept everywhere and that its earlier removal was an error: every address book list and every address picker pages, and no requirement says a list of an organisation's addresses is served or shown unpaginated. It drops req-611's 'unpaginated' clause and supersedes ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 on that point alone, because that point's reasoning rested on the address book's list endpoint taking no role and so having to be read whole and paged for display, which is no longer true of the service: RequestedListFilters takes roles and searchRoles, AddressController lists one page at a time with page and pageSize, and ListPaging sets 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, exactly the bounds ruling:paul-2026-11-05 point 8 names. The role filter runs in the service before the page is cut, so paging the API cannot make it wrong, and Paul's point 8 stands in full. The rest of ruling:ian-2026-11-23 stands: the pickers page at eight, the one-page clause of inc-087's criteria 7, 8 and 9 stays dropped with req-594 and req-595, and the 'Selected address' restatement comes back with the paging. EUDPA-827 is the fix and has landed on the animals frontend's main. It settles conflict c-292 by keeping the plants contact picker's pagination and inset, and the contact picker pages at eight rather than five, confirmed by Ian the same day, so every picker in both journeys pages at the figure the INS address book list already uses and ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 1 set for the other pickers.

sources.role: the decision on transporter management, outranking ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm on that point and lifting claim c-285: the address book manages transporters as per-organisation records, and adding one mid journey uses the address book hand-off already built for addresses (inc-077, inc-078, inc-080). A transporter is its own record in its own transporters collection inside the address book service, not the Address model; it has no roles and stores a private-or-commercial type instead; a commercial transporter country is forced to XI (Northern Ireland) with no reference-data lookup, while a private transporter keeps its choice of export country. Approved transporters are parked.

claims.statement: This ruling settles whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does - the question ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 (claim c-285) left blocked pending requirements.
claims.quote: On transporter management, which Sam's ruling of 9 October (afternoon) left blocked pending requirements — whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does (`ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm` point 5, claim c-285):
claims.note: answers the block ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 left, recorded there as claim c-285

claims.statement: The address book manages transporters, which are saved per organisation just like other addresses.
claims.quote: My decision is that the address book will manage the transporters, just like other addresses which are saved per organisation.

claims.statement: Adding a transporter uses the same pattern of moving to the address book mid journey that adding other addresses uses.
claims.quote: It will use the same pattern with moving to the address book mid journey, like other addresses when adding transporters - it's essentially the same pattern.

claims.statement: The earlier block rested on the concept of 'approved transporters': a list that may be managed in MDM for all organisations and added to each organisation's own transporter options.
claims.quote: I think that previous ruling was based on the concept of 'approved transporters' which may be a list managed in MDM for all organisations that will be added to the organisations individual transporter options.

claims.statement: Approved transporters are not to be worried about for now.

sources.role: the decision on what the address book stores for an address's type and uses (EUDPA-711): "use" is renamed "role" everywhere, in the record, the API, the code, the copy keys, the tests and the spec, and an address holds the roles it can play on a notification, being place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination and branch address. The address book stores roles only and requires at least one; it does not store an address type and ignores one a client sends, the address type being the INS front door's grouping of roles worked out from them. The grouping of roles into sending, receiving and branch is the address book's internal rule rather than part of its API, and it refuses roles from more than one group, and a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom. The list takes role, repeatable and any-of, and searchRole, in place of addressType, use and searchUse. A role a new notification type needs is added in code, each role in exactly one group. Addresses saved before the change are not migrated: after release the addresses collection is dropped in dev and test with CDP tooling and the address book restarted, and locally the stack is restarted. The address book's list and every address picker keep pagination even though the Design Release 2.1 prototype has none, the list API paging with page and pageSize of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, because organisations in test environments hold thousands of addresses; no requirement to list an organisation's addresses unpaginated is built, which ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 later reads the other way for req-611 and so outranks on that point alone.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that, as a pre-step for these increments, three questions are answered: is it possible with off-the-shelf GDS; if not, with other complementary off-the-shelf components; if not, why is the atypical thing strongly required. claims.note: New.

claims.quote: Raise one only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the default nor DR1 settles it.
claims.note: New. Both conditions must hold. 'The default' is read as the prototype-wins default from the Precedence paragraph.

claims.statement: Increments are grouped into themes, and the themes are drawn from the evidence.
claims.quote: Themes: group the increments into themes based on the evidence.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Each theme's boundary is set by the code it touches.
claims.quote: Draw the boundaries by the code each one touches
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without pull requests that conflict with each other.
claims.quote: so themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without conflicting PRs.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

claims.statement: The service exposes a commodity search at GET /commodities, described as searching species by name or commodity code.
claims.quote: @RequestMapping("/commodities") ... @Operation(summary = "Search species by name or commodity code"

claims.statement: The commodity endpoints are tagged as serving live-animal commodity codes and species from MDM.
claims.quote: @Tag(name = "Commodities", description = "Live-animal commodity codes and species from MDM")

claims.statement: GET /commodities takes an optional search term in the query parameter q, which may be a species name or a commodity code.
claims.quote: @Parameter(description = "Search term: a species name or a commodity code", example = "dog") @RequestParam(value = "q", required = false) String q

claims.statement: GET /commodities takes a zero-based page number in the query parameter page, defaulting to 0 and refusing anything below 0.
claims.quote: @Parameter(description = "Zero-based page number") @RequestParam(defaultValue = "0") @Min(0) int page

claims.statement: GET /commodities takes the most species to list in the query parameter size, defaulting to 100 and limited to between 1 and 100.
claims.quote: @Parameter(description = "Most species to list, from 1 to 100") @RequestParam(defaultValue = "100") @Min(1) @Max(CommoditySearchService.MAXIMUM_PAGE_SIZE) int size ... static final int MAXIMUM_PAGE_SIZE = 100;

claims.statement: GET /commodities answers 400 when the page or size is not valid, 503 when MDM is unavailable, and 200 with the matching species otherwise.
claims.quote: @ApiResponse(responseCode = "200", description = "The matching species") @ApiResponse(responseCode = "400", description = "The page or size is not valid") @ApiResponse(responseCode = "503", description = "MDM unavailable")

claims.statement: The search term is trimmed of surrounding spaces before it is used, and a missing term counts as empty.
claims.quote: String trimmedSearchTerm = searchTerm == null ? "" : searchTerm.trim();

claims.statement: A trimmed search term shorter than two characters matches nothing: the search answers 200 with a total of 0, the page and size asked for, and no groups, without asking MDM.
claims.quote: static final int MINIMUM_SEARCH_LENGTH = 2; ... if (trimmedSearchTerm.length() < MINIMUM_SEARCH_LENGTH) { ... return CommoditySearchResponse.builder().total(0).page(page).size(size).groups(List.of()).build(); ... "A term shorter than two characters matches nothing."

claims.statement: A search term of two characters or more is sent to MDM's product search with the page and size the caller gave.
claims.quote: mdmService.searchProducts(trimmedSearchTerm, page, size);

claims.statement: The service does not itself tell a search by commodity code apart from a search by species name: both go to MDM's one product search as the same q term, and MDM's answer decides whether species rows or commodity rows come back.
claims.quote: @GetMapping(value = "/mdm/trade/product/search") ... @RequestParam(value = "q") String query
claims.note: Inferred from the absence of any code-versus-name branch in CommoditySearchService; the IT shows a q of 0102 returning a commodity row and q of dog, cattle or bison returning species rows.

claims.statement: MDM product search returns two kinds of row, species and commodity; a row of any other result type is read as having no type and contributes nothing to the search.
claims.quote: @JsonFormat(with = JsonFormat.Feature.READ_UNKNOWN_ENUM_VALUES_AS_NULL) ResultType resultType ... @JsonProperty("species") SPECIES, @JsonProperty("commodity") COMMODITY ... return null;
claims.note: mechanism: maps MDM product search rows to a commodity code by result type.

claims.statement: A species row from MDM search becomes one species match under the row's commodityCnCode, with the row's speciesName as the Latin name and its commonName.
claims.quote: if (row.resultType() == SPECIES) { return row.commodityCnCode(); } ... Stream.of(new SpeciesMatch(code, row.latinName(), row.commonName())); ... @JsonProperty("speciesName") String latinName
claims.note: mechanism: turns MDM species search rows into code and species pairs.

claims.statement: A commodity row from MDM search contributes one species match per entry in its scientificNames list, each under the row's code; a commodity row with no scientificNames contributes nothing.
claims.quote: if (row.resultType() == COMMODITY) { return row.code(); } ... if (row.species() == null) { return Stream.empty(); } ... @JsonProperty("scientificNames") List<MdmSpecies> species
claims.note: mechanism: expands an MDM commodity search row into its listed species.

claims.statement: An MDM search row with no commodity code (no commodityCnCode on a species row, no code on a commodity row, or no result type) is left out of the search.
claims.quote: String code = codeOf(row); if (code == null) { return Stream.empty(); }
claims.note: mechanism: drops MDM search rows that carry no commodity code.

claims.statement: After each search, the service asks MDM once for the commodity records of every distinct code the search rows carry, and leaves out every row whose code MDM flags as germinal (isGerminal true).
claims.quote: return mdmService.getCommodities(codes).stream().filter(CommoditySearchService::isGerminal) ... return Boolean.TRUE.equals(commodity.isGerminal()); ... .filter(row -> !germinalCodes.contains(codeOf(row)))

claims.statement: A code MDM does not flag as germinal is listed even when it sits outside the live-animals chapter; a missing isGerminal counts as not germinal.
claims.quote: search_listsACodeOutsideTheLiveAnimalsChapter_whenMdmDoesNotFlagItGerminal ... givenMdmCommodities(commodity("0102", false), commodity("05111000", null));

claims.statement: A species with no Latin name is left out of the search results.
claims.quote: .filter(match -> match.latinName() != null)

claims.statement: The same species (same Latin name) under the same code is listed once, keeping the first occurrence's common name, even when MDM returns it on both a species row and a commodity row.
claims.quote: matchesByCodeAndLatinName.putIfAbsent(List.of(match.code(), match.latinName()), match)
claims.note: mechanism: de-duplicates MDM species matches by commodity code and Latin name.

claims.statement: The same species under two different codes is listed under each code, so one species can appear in several groups.
claims.quote: searchCommodities_groupsMdmSpeciesRowsUnderTheirCodes ... .code("01061900").species(List.of(species("Bison bonasus", "European Bison")))

claims.statement: The search lists no more species than the size asked for, in MDM's order, but its total counts every distinct named, non-germinal species match on the MDM page it read.
claims.quote: List<SpeciesMatch> listed = matches.stream().limit(size).toList(); ... .total(matches.size())

claims.statement: The search total is the number of species matches on the one MDM page read, not MDM's totalElements, so it does not count matches on later MDM pages.
claims.quote: .total(matches.size()) ... assertThat(response.getBody().total()).isEqualTo(15); ... "totalElements": 1
claims.note: Inferred: totalElements of the MDM search page is never read by CommoditySearchService; the 0102 fixture has totalElements 1 and the endpoint answers total 15. The schema text 'Number of species matching the search term' is therefore true only of the page read. MDM pages are of rows (a commodity row can hold many species), so page and size mean different units to MDM and to this service.

claims.statement: Matching species are grouped by commodity code, with the groups and the species within each group in the order MDM returned them.
claims.quote: Collectors.groupingBy(SpeciesMatch::code, LinkedHashMap::new, ... "Species on this page, grouped by commodity code in MDM's order"

claims.statement: The search response has four required fields: total (number of species matching the term), page (zero-based page number), size (most species the page lists) and groups (species on this page grouped by commodity code).
claims.quote: "Number of species matching the search term" ... long total, ... "Zero-based page number" ... int page, ... "Most species the page lists" ... int size, ... List<CommodityGroup> groups

claims.statement: The search response echoes the page and size the caller asked for.
claims.quote: .page(page) .size(size)

claims.statement: A commodity group has a required commodity (CN) code, such as 0102, and the list of matching species under that code.
claims.quote: "Commodity (CN) code", requiredMode = REQUIRED, example = "0102") String code, @Schema(description = "Matching species listed under the code", requiredMode = REQUIRED) List<CommoditySpecies> species

claims.statement: A species in the search has a required Latin (scientific) name, such as Bos taurus, and a common name, such as Cattle or Cow, which is null when MDM holds none.
claims.quote: "Latin (scientific) name", requiredMode = REQUIRED, example = "Bos taurus") String latinName, @Schema(description = "Common name, when MDM holds one", requiredMode = NOT_REQUIRED, types = {"string", "null"}, example = "Cattle or Cow") @Nullable String commonName

claims.statement: The search response gives each group only its commodity code: it carries no commodity description (such as MDM's "Live bovine animals"), selectability or hierarchy, though MDM returns them.
claims.note: Looked in CommodityGroup, CommoditySearchResponse and MdmProductSearchResult: no description, isSelectable, parentCode or children field is read or returned. A page showing a commodity name beside the code has no source in this service today.

claims.statement: Each GET /commodities call is counted as a commodity-search lookup in the service's lookup metric.
claims.quote: lookupMetrics.recordLookup(LookupMetrics.COMMODITY_SEARCH); ... assertThat(lookupTypesCounted()).containsExactly("commodity-search");

claims.statement: A search logs, at info, how many MDM rows it left out for having no code, how many species for having no Latin name and how many beyond the page size, and logs the germinal codes it left out.
claims.quote: "Commodity search for '{}' leaves out {} MDM rows with no code, {} species with no " + "Latin name and {} species beyond the page size" ... "Commodity search for '{}' leaves out germinal codes {}"

claims.statement: The service exposes a species check at POST /commodities/species-check, which returns the lines whose Latin name MDM does not list under their code.
claims.quote: @Operation(summary = "Check chosen species are still listed under their codes", description = "Returns the lines whose Latin name MDM does not list under their code.") ... @PostMapping("/species-check")

claims.statement: The species check answers 200 with the lines MDM does not list, 400 when the body is not a list of complete lines, and 503 when MDM is unavailable.
claims.quote: @ApiResponse(responseCode = "200", description = "The lines MDM does not list") @ApiResponse(responseCode = "400", description = "The body is not a list of complete lines") @ApiResponse(responseCode = "503", description = "MDM unavailable")

claims.statement: The species check request has one required field, lines: the commodity lines whose species to check against MDM.
claims.quote: "Commodity lines whose species to check against MDM", requiredMode = REQUIRED) @NotNull @Valid List<CommodityLine> lines

claims.statement: A commodity line is a species chosen under a commodity code, with a required, non-blank commodity (CN) code and a required, non-blank Latin name.
claims.quote: @Schema(description = "A species chosen under a commodity code") ... "Commodity (CN) code", requiredMode = REQUIRED, example = "0102") @NotBlank String code, ... "Latin (scientific) name of the species", requiredMode = REQUIRED, example = "Bos taurus") @NotBlank String latinName

claims.statement: The species check response has one required field, unlisted: the lines whose species MDM does not list under their code, in the order they were sent.
claims.quote: "Lines whose species MDM does not list under their code", requiredMode = REQUIRED) List<CommodityLine> unlisted ... request.lines().stream().filter(line -> !isListed(line, latinNamesByCode)).toList();

claims.statement: A line is listed when its Latin name exactly matches, case included, a species name MDM lists under the line's code; otherwise it is returned as unlisted.
